newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima says sets course for restructuring pact.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima says sets course for restructuring pact.

text.p: Japan's Tobishima Corp announced on Friday that it has set a clear course for a basic agreement with its creditor banks on its restructuring plan.

"By today, we have sat a clear course for reaching a basic agreement with all private financial institutions concerned (on a restructuring plan announced last October)," the troubled construction firm said in a statement.
It added that negotiations with public financial firms would continue, but it did not elaborate.

Under the restructuring plan formed last year, debt-ridden Tobishima asked its creditors to reduce their claims against the construction firm for its group companies' debt to 100 billion yen from about 740 billion yen.
There are more than 50 creditor financial institutions, of which Fuji Bank Ltd is the main creditor.

Tobishima president Shoichiro Ishihara, meanwhile, told a news conference on Friday that a final agreement is likely to be reached in early April on the restructuring plan, which he said should include a cut in creditor banks' claims against Tobishima for its group firms' debts as originally planned.

Tobishima topped the list of Japanese builders which have guaranteed huge loans which may not be recoverable, as of the end of last September, according to leading credit research firm Teikoku Databank Ltd.
Japan's constructors were active participants in Japan's 1980s "bubble" era of skyrocketing asset prices, and were left with heaps of bad loans after the bubble burst in early 1990.
Builders led the bubble-era investment in property and real estate and also guaranteed their real estate units' loans.
